data.title: Google Partner Novacore Labs and AIBotics Complete Acquisition of Assets, Expanding AI, Drone, Mapping and Automation Platform in Jamaica
data.description:
Asset acquisition adds the NovaCore brand, intellectual property, software, customer data, contracts, drone and mapping assets, and operating capabilities positioned for growth across Jamaica and the broader Caribbean

NovaCore intends to expand institutional programs with the University of the West Indies Global Campus and the University of Technology through its relationship with PlayJamaica Limited

MIAMI and KINGSTON, Jamaica, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AIBotics, Inc. ( AIBT ) ("AIBotics" or the "Company"), a global technology company building a platform around AI-enabled robotics, autonomous systems and intelligent automation, today announced the completion of its acquisition of the operating assets associated with NovaCore Labs ("NovaCore") from PlayJamaica Limited under an Asset Sale and Purchase Agreement.

The transaction provides AIBotics ( AIBT ) with a tangible operating platform to complete its expansion plans in Jamaica and the CARICOM. The Caribbean Economic Outlook 2026 projects a combined regional GDP of approximately US$420 billion with an average real GDP growth rate of 3.4% across major economies.

The acquired assets include 10 service robots, six commercial drones, three field generators, Google Street View mapping equipment and a dedicated mapping vehicle, together with the NovaCore brand and proprietary operating methodologies.

The acquisition expands AIBotics’ technology platform and operating presence in Jamaica while creating a foundation for broader growth across the CARICOM region. Through NovaCore, AIBotics ( AIBT ) intends to build on established capabilities in AI-enabled mapping and geospatial services, drone operations, automation, digital infrastructure, institutional technology programs and workforce development, with the goal of creating a scalable regional technology platform.

Ben Kaplan, Chief Executive Officer of AIBotics ( AIBT ), commented, "NovaCore has established a presence in Jamaica through Google-related mapping initiatives, commercial technology deployments and relationships with leading academic and institutional organizations. Those capabilities can provide a practical platform for converting technology into recurring commercial activity rather than building a Caribbean operation from the ground up.

Following the acquisition, NovaCore intends to prioritize the expansion of business lines that present near-term revenue opportunities in Jamaica and the broader region. These initiatives include:

• AI, LiDAR and geospatial services: Building on NovaCore's mapping work, the business plans to expand into AI- and LiDAR-enabled asset management, surface classification and related geospatial services for public- and private-sector applications.

• Drone services: NovaCore intends to broaden commercial drone operations across selected public- and private-sector verticals, supported by acquired drone systems, field equipment, operating methodologies and drone-management software.

• Automation and robotics: The acquired asset package includes robotics equipment, operating methodologies, software and customer relationships that can support continued automation deployments across commercial environments.

• Education and workforce development: NovaCore intends to expand institutional programs with the University of the West Indies Global Campus and the University of Technology, including technical demonstrations, training, apprenticeship and internship initiatives designed to build local technical capacity.

• Technical infrastructure: NovaCore intends to expand its technical laboratory capabilities to support demonstrations, deployments, customer workflows and the development of a skilled regional workforce.

Under the Asset Sale and Purchase Agreement, AIBotics ( AIBT ) acquired the specified NovaCore assets from PlayJamaica Limited in exchange for 22,500 shares of AIBotics Series B Preferred Stock with an aggregate stated value of $225,000.

The agreement also provides for an earn-out of up to $3.0 million in additional Series B Preferred Stock over four years if the acquired business achieves specified cumulative gross-revenue milestones of $500,000, $1.5 million, $3.0 million and $5.0 million. Each revenue milestone corresponds to $750,000 of additional preferred-stock consideration.

Under the terms of the agreement, Gregory Moore is to lead the acquired business as President of the operating subsidiary. AIBotics ( AIBT ) and Moore are also to develop a budget targeting $1.0 million of capital deployment over a 12-month period.

Gregory Moore, co-founder of NovaCore Labs, commented, "This transaction gives NovaCore the opportunity to accelerate the work already underway in mapping, drones, automation, AI and institutional technology programs. Our focus now is execution - expanding services, deepening our technical capabilities, building revenue and creating solutions that can be deployed across Jamaica and the wider Caribbean."

Mr. Kaplan added, “NovaCore represents an important step in AIBotics’ evolution into a broader international technology platform. By expanding our presence in Jamaica and the Caribbean, we believe we can build meaningful businesses across AI, robotics, drones, mapping and automation while creating a foundation for long-term regional growth.”

NovaCore previously participated in Jamaica's Google Street View mapping initiative, providing a foundation for broader geospatial and digital-infrastructure applications. Management now intends to build on that work by incorporating AI and LiDAR technologies into services designed for asset management, surface classification, infrastructure analysis and other data-driven applications.

NovaCore also maintains relationships with the University of Technology and the University of the West Indies Global Campus. The Company intends to use those relationships to support training, demonstrations, workforce development and selected immersive-learning and simulation initiatives, while expanding the technical infrastructure available for client deployments and operational support.

AIBotics ( AIBT ) does not intend to identify public-sector agencies involved in active tender, evaluation or procurement processes unless and until disclosure is appropriate and authorized.

AIBotics ( AIBT ) seeks to identify, develop, implement and scale solutions that improve how machines operate, automate business processes and extend the practical application of artificial intelligence into the physical world. data.title: CANADA STOCKS-TSX rises as oil stocks gain on Brent touching $110 a barrel
data.description:
(Updates to close)

Oct 16 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index gained on Friday, boosted by oil stocks, while investors assessed Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem's warning on persistent energy-price pressures on interest rates.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index gained 0.11% to 36,176.55, touching its highest level since September 4. The index gained 1.44% in the week.

* Energy stocks rose 2.8%. Brent touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May on worries that escalating tensions in the Middle East could further tighten supplies.

* South of the border, Wall Street ended sharply lower, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure.

* In Canada, technology stocks fell 3.5%, dragged down by a 5% fall in Shopify ( SHOP ) and 7.7% decline in BlackBerry.

* "It's (AI trade) probably affecting the TSX to a significantly lesser extent than it's affecting some of the US indices... there's a pretty big disparity between tech and everything else at the moment," said Josh Sheluk, CIO at Verecan Capital Management.

* "The TSX offers a pretty interesting diversifying investment relative to global stocks because it is a lot more heavily allocated and weighted towards not only energy but materials as well," Sheluk said.

* Macklem said Canada has not raised interest rates yet but the longer elevated energy prices go on "the harder that gets".

* The BoC is not expected to raise interest rates at its next monetary policy decision announcement on October 28, but money markets are pricing in a rate hike of 25 basis points in December, according to data compiled by LSEG.

* Data on the day showed that Canadian home sales extended their decline in September, after a drop in August, as higher mortgage rates and expectations of a rate hike weighed on demand.

(Reporting by Anand Gopal and Nivedita Balu in Bengaluru; Editing by Shreya Biswas and Nia Williams)

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall Street ends down sharply, worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
data.description:
(Updates with closing stock moves)

* Chips, AI infrastructure companies fall as debt concerns linger

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq suffer steepest weekly losses since June

* Tesla dips after unveiling electric sports car

* S&P 500 -1.09%, Nasdaq -2.15%, Dow -0.34%

By Noel Randewich

Oct 16 (Reuters) - Wall Street ended sharply lower on Friday, with CoreWeave ( CRWV ), Broadcom ( AVGO ) and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.

The Nasdaq extended losses from earlier in the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise.

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave ( CRWV ) slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

Broadcom ( AVGO ) fell 4.5%, and the PHLX chip index sank 3.8% in its eighth straight day of declines, its longest losing streak since 2008.

Investors on Friday were also watching oil prices jump more than 3% due to Middle East supply worries.

"There is some fear in the market," said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at U.S. Bank Wealth Management in ​Seattle. "High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk."

Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The S&P 500 declined 1.09% to end the session at 7,659.44 points.

The Nasdaq declined 2.15% to 26,140.03 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.34% to 52,002.41 points.

Reflecting a rotation from tech stocks into other areas of the stock market, six of the S&P 500's 11 sector indexes rose, led by energy, up 2.47%, followed by a 1.4% gain in utilities.

Volume on US exchanges was relatively heavy, with 18.6 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.7 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell almost 1.95% and the Nasdaq slumped 4.48%, their deepest weekly declines since June. The Dow climbed 0.67% for the week.

Third-quarter earnings season shifts into high gear next week with reports from Tesla, Meta Platforms ( META ) and Procter & Gamble. Analysts on average see quarterly earnings surging more than 30%, driven by AI-related megacaps, according to LSEG data.

While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2026, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index's median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date. About 185 S&P 500 stocks have lost ground in 2026.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week showed price pressures were extending beyond energy commodities.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday voiced optimism about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" during a lingering energy shock and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation.

Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January.

Tesla dropped 3.1% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX.

Netflix ( NFLX ) appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares dipped 2.8%.

Declining stocks roughly matched rising ones within the S&P 500..

The S&P 500 posted 19 new highs and one new low; the Nasdaq recorded 51 new highs and 353 new lows.

(Reporting by Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru, and by Noel Randewich in San Francisco; additional reporting by Vidya Ranganathan; Editing by Joyjeet Das, Shinjini Ganguli and David Gregorio)

data.title: Update: US Equity Indexes Retreat Amid Rotation Out of High-Growth Sectors, Surge in Crude Oil
data.description:
04:41 PM EDT, 10/16/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with index/price moves, macroeconomic data, and company/geopolitical news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes closed lower on Friday as semiconductor and software stocks led mega-cap declines amid a rotation out of long-duration sectors while crude oil surged.

The Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.2% to 26,140.03, and the S&P 500 declined 1.1% to 7,659.44. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.3% to 52,022.41, after trading higher earlier in the session.

Technology, communication services and consumer discretionary were among the worst performers. Energy, utilities, and consumer staples topped the gainers. Technology is poised to hit the bottom of sector charts this week, while consumer defensive is emerging as the leader.

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) co-founders Michael Intrator, Brian Venturo and Brannin McBee have sold $3.3 billion in company shares since its March 2025 initial public offering, including $2.4 billion in 2026, Bloomberg reported. Shares sank 12%, extending losses from earlier this week as concern mounted around its debt and credit risk.

The PHLX Semiconductor index slumped 3.8%, sliding for the eighth straight day amid jitters surrounding the so-called AI trade. Sixteen of the bottom 20 names among stocks with market capitalization exceeding $200 billion were technology firms, according to data compiled by Finviz. The remaining four were all communication services companies. Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) led decliners in this mega-cap category, down 7.6%.

In geopolitical news, US lawmakers introduced a bill to block President Donald Trump's deal with Russia to release several hundred million barrels of diesel, Bloomberg reported.

Separately, Trump said the US may have to target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain as he seeks to ensure Tehran does not get a nuclear weapon, Reuters reported. Iranian Acting Oil Minister Hamid Bovard has said the country "will take precise, appropriate retaliatory measures at the right time to counter enemy threats" to its energy facilities, Al Jazeera, a Middle Eastern broadcaster, reported.

The front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract jumped 3.6% to $101.46 per barrel, while global benchmark Brent advanced 3.5% to $109.59 per barrel.

In economic news, industrial production rose 0.7% in September, versus expectations for 0.4% in a Bloomberg-compiled poll, and following an upwardly revised 0.1% increase in August, according to the Federal Reserve.

The New York Federal Reserve's services index fell to minus 20.7 in October from minus 8.7 in September, compared with the minus 4.1 forecast in a survey compiled by Bloomberg. The index is the first services sector reading for October and suggests widespread contraction.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh avoided signaling the Fed's next monetary policy moves but reaffirmed its commitment to price stability, according to a Commerzbank note. Warsh, however, sees a significant investment boom driven by artificial intelligence, per the research note.

Most US Treasury yields fell, seesawing in the final leg of trading. The two-year rate dropped 3.4 basis points to 4.72%, and the 10-year yield slipped by less than one basis point to 5.08%. The 30-year rate climbed less than one basis point to 5.43%.

data.title: US Equity Indexes Mixed This Week as CoreWeave Rattles AI Trade, Sparks Rotation Out of Technology
data.description:
04:29 PM EDT, 10/16/2026 (MT Newswires) -- US equity indexes closed mixed as a rotation out of technology amid AI jitters outweighed hotter-than-expected inflation prints this week.

* The S&P 500 closed at 7,659.44 on Friday, versus 7,815.31 a week ago. The Nasdaq Composite stood at about 26,140.03, compared with 27,372.43 a week earlier. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended at 52,002.41, relative to 51,718.50 last week.

* Technology hit the bottom of sector charts, while consumer defensive emerged as the leader.

* This week, 17 of the bottom 20 names among stocks with a market capitalization exceeding $200 billion were from technology, according to data compiled by Finviz.

* The cost of protecting CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) debt against default for five years rose to 1194.5 basis points Thursday, an intraday record, with swaps pricing in a chance of default at over 60% within the next five years, Bloomberg reported, citing data from ICE Data Services.

* Bloomberg reported CoreWeave ( CRWV ) co-founders Michael Intrator, Brian Venturo and Brannin McBee sold $3.3 billion of the firm's shares since its March 2025 initial public offering, including $2.4 billion in 2026. CoreWeave ( CRWV ) shares sank 25% this week amid debt and credit risk concerns, which triggered a 25% sell-off in Nebius ( NBIS ) , a 23% plunge in IREN (IREN), and a 9.3% drop in Oracle (ORCL) over the past five days.

* September's hotter-than-expected core consumer price inflation and the fastest growth in producer prices in more than four years failed to spark a rally in US Treasury yields. The 10- and 30-year yields ended the week lower after rates sank on Wednesday and Thursday when consumer and producer prices were released.

* Reflecting the downward movement in yields, the probability of the Federal Reserve leaving its target rate unchanged in October stood at 83%, up from 51% a month ago. The increase came entirely at the expense of the Fed raising rates by 25 basis points.

data.title: Hyperscale Data Announces Plan for its askROI Subsidiary to Go Public in the Second or Third Quarter of 2027
data.description:
askROI Offers an All-in-One Platform Featuring More Than 240 Productivity Tools, Generative AI, Business Automation and Advanced AI Research

LAS VEGAS, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data ( GPUS/PD ), Inc. , an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data ( GPUS/PD )" or the "Company"), today announced that its subsidiary, askROI, Inc. ("askROI"), an AI technology company, is preparing to become a separate, publicly traded company, whether through a reverse takeover ("RTO"), an initial public offering of askROI's securities ("IPO"), or through the use of a special purpose acquisition company (a "SPAC" and collectively with the RTO and the IPO, a "Transaction"). The Company and askROI are targeting a consummated Transaction by the second or third quarter of 2027, depending upon the type of transaction that the Company ultimately determines to pursue, and if the Transaction constitutes an RTO, the completion of the subsequent filing of a resale registration statement registering the shares of the current public company, which has not been identified, that the Company would receive in the RTO in consideration for the Company's sale of askROI to it in the first half of 2027, subject to the completion of necessary financial and regulatory requirements, as well as prevailing market conditions.

askROI is an AI technology company offering an all-in-one AI productivity, research, automation and content creation platform. Available through web and mobile applications, askROI provides access to leading AI models, more than 240 productivity tools, custom AI applications, enterprise knowledge management capabilities and generative AI technologies. The platform serves individuals, entrepreneurs, professionals and businesses seeking to leverage artificial intelligence to improve productivity, automate workflows and accelerate innovation. For more information, visit www.askROI.com.

The intended public listing represents another step in Hyperscale Data's ( GPUS/PD ) broader strategy to unlock stockholder value by positioning its operating businesses to pursue independent growth opportunities and establish separate market valuations.

In connection with the preparation of the Transaction, Milton "Todd" Ault III will step down as Chief Executive Officer of askROI and askROI is expected to appoint Joseph Spaziano as Chief Executive Officer and Ryan Doucette as President. Mr. Spaziano, who currently serves as Chief Technology Officer of Hyperscale Data ( GPUS/PD ), as well as President and Chief Operating Officer of askROI, would step down from his role at Hyperscale Data ( GPUS/PD ) to focus solely on askROI. Mr. Doucette currently serves as Head of Product at askROI. The Company currently anticipates, but cannot state with any certainty, that Messrs. Spaziano and Doucette would continue in these positions subsequent to any Transaction.

The planned leadership transition is intended to provide askROI with a dedicated management team focused on scaling its AI platform and positioning the company for independent operations.

Milton "Todd" Ault III, Founder and Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data ( GPUS/PD ), commented: "We believe there is incredible value in askROI, which is currently not being recognized by the public markets while it is a subsidiary of Hyperscale Data ( GPUS/PD ). We also believe comparable AI technology companies often trade at substantially higher valuations, and we further believe that the stockholders of the Company would benefit from having askROI be a separate entity and have the ability to establish its own independent market value since we expect that such a separation could enhance the market capitalization of the Company by virtue of its ownership of a post-Transaction public entity. Finally, we expect this planned public listing can benefit Hyperscale Data ( GPUS/PD ) stockholders, as well as future askROI shareholders, by providing greater transparency into the value of the business while creating a platform for future growth, access to capital and long-term shareholder value creation."

The Company expects to provide additional information regarding the transaction structure, corporate organization and listing timetable for the planned public listing of askROI at a later date. There can be no assurance that the proposed public listing will occur within the anticipated timeframe or at all.

The planned public listing of askROI is consistent with Hyperscale Data's ( GPUS/PD ) broader strategy of evaluating opportunities to establish independent market valuations for its portfolio businesses. Management believes that separating certain operating businesses into independently valued enterprises could provide investors with greater transparency into the underlying assets and operations of Hyperscale Data ( GPUS/PD ). The Company intends to continue evaluating strategic alternatives for its subsidiaries and investments as it seeks to maximize long-term stockholder value.

data.title: SoftBank weighs $18 billion acquisition of Allied Universal, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - SoftBank Group is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal in a deal that could value the US security services provider at about $18 billion, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

-- Allied Universal provides security staffing for businesses, venues and major events, and has a growing presence in the data center industry, supporting both development and operation of facilities

-- The potential acquisition would complement SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son's increasing focus on AI, as he is exploring the use of AI-powered robots across industries, and looking to strengthen the infrastructure needed to support the technology, according to the report

-- With Allied, SoftBank would look to eventually replace some staff with robots to handle security work, the report said, citing one of the people

-- The application of humanoid-like security workers will likely take more time, it reported citing another person

-- Deliberations are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, including on the potential price, the report said

-- SoftBank declined to comment on the report, while Allied Universal did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment

-- SoftBank is widely known for making large technology investments through its Vision Fund. It was an early investor in Alibaba, owns a majority stake in Arm, and was a major backer of the office-sharing startup WeWork

-- In October, SoftBank completed the final phase of its planned $30 billion investment in OpenAI, deepening its commitment to the AI company

(Reporting by Apratim Sarkar in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar)

data.description:
(Updates headline and prices throughout, adds oil settlement)

* US dollar heads for weekly loss on lower US Treasury yields

* Bond markets stabilise after rush for safe havens on Thursday

* Investors worry about debt risks in AI-related stocks

By Chibuike Oguh and Elizabeth Howcroft

NEW YORK/PARIS, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Global stocks fell modestly on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.

Markets have been rattled this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks.

Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after stronger-than-expected inflation data was released on Wednesday, while investors piled into Treasuries and other government bonds.

On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were trading down and were headed for weekly losses. The Dow was lower after reversing early gains but was still set for a weekly gain.

Technology and communication services were driving losses while the top gainers were utilities and energy stocks.

CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) shares shed 13% and were on track to lose nearly 26% this week amid increasing investor scrutiny of the financing for the massive AI infrastructure buildout.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.57%, the S&P 500 lost 1.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.3%.

The MSCI World Equity Index lost 0.54% and was set for a weekly loss. European stock indexes, hit less hard by Thursday's selloff, gained, with the STOXX 600 adding 0.72%. London's FTSE 100 rose 0.38%.

"We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," said Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund.

"Our view is that there's going to be some really significant winners. But you have to be careful on the financing capability because companies don't get into trouble because their assets don't exceed their liabilities. They get into trouble when they have liquidity issues."

Asian stocks mostly rose, and bond markets steadied, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves.

Indonesian equities suffered their biggest drop since 1998 after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging-market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds.

DOLLAR FALLS, BONDS RECOVER

The dollar index fell 0.21% and was on track for its first weekly decline after four weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, analysts said.

The euro rose from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.1% at $1.12315.

The Japanese yen weakened 0.03% against the greenback to 158.05 per dollar.

European government bond yields edged higher, while US bond yields reversed earlier declines. Germany's 10-year yield rose 4.36 basis points to 3.453%. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 2.13 basis points to 5.108%.

Even so, yields have eased this week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May.

Brent crude futures rose 3.72% to settle at $109.86 a barrel and were headed for a second straight weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have surged in the past 10 days.

Gold gained support from the weaker dollar, rising 0.25% to $4,159.69 an ounce.

data.title: FAA set to approve Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week, sources say
data.description:
* FAA completed key Type Certification Board safety review on Friday, sources say

* Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, about 30% of 737 backlog

* FAA said October 2 navigation software glitch posed no safety concern

By David Shepardson and Dan Catchpole

WASHINGTON, Oct 16 (Reuters) - The Federal Aviation Administration is set to approve the long-delayed Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week, after completing a key safety review on Friday, three people familiar with the matter said.

The review by the Type Certification Board - made up of FAA management team members - is a final step before the agency decides on certification. The MAX 10 is a larger variant of Boeing's ( BA ) best-selling 737 MAX and its expected approval marks a key milestone for the US planemaker.

Boeing ( BA ) has faced a more stringent certification process since two fatal MAX 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019, as well as scrutiny of the company's production and quality systems after a January 2024 mid-air cabin panel blowout on a nearly new Alaska Airlines MAX 9.

Asked for comment, the FAA said, "Safety dictates the certification timeline." Boeing ( BA ) referred questions to the FAA.

The FAA in August gave long-awaited ​approval to the smaller 737 MAX 7 after reviewing the plane for more than eight years. Boeing ( BA ) at one point planned to start delivering the MAX 10 in 2020.

A problem with the anti-ice system on 737 MAX engines that arose in 2023 further delayed certification of the MAX 7 and 10.

The delays have helped European rival Airbus' A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market. Boeing ( BA ) has said the MAX 10 will be a major cash-flow driver in its ongoing financial recovery following years of crises and controversies.

Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for about 30% of Boeing's ( BA ) outstanding 737 backlog. The planemaker has already built a handful of MAX 10s awaiting delivery.

The bigger plane that can carry more passengers is crucial to several airlines' growth plans. Major customers for the MAX 10 include United Airlines, Alaska, Ryanair, Delta Air Lines ( DAL ) and American Airlines ( AAL ).

A glitch with the latest update of the 737 MAX's navigation software threatened to further delay certification when Boeing ( BA ) disclosed it in late September. However, the FAA determined on October 2 that it did not pose a safety concern and did not require Boeing ( BA ) to fix the problem as a condition of certifying the plane.

Boeing ( BA ) is still working on certifying the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production, which is already six years behind schedule. The company has said it expects to complete certification and begin deliveries in 2027.

(Reporting by David Shepardson in Washington and Dan Catchpole in Seattle; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Avenue Capital emerges as frontrunner for stake in Serie A media rights venture, sources say
data.description:
* Targets 10% stake for €320 million as common equity, sources say

* Offer emerged as best option at Friday's meeting, sources say

* Rival bid pegs higher valuation under structured equity deal,

* sources say

* Bids to examined further in coming weeks, sources say

*

By Elvira Pollina

MILAN, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Private equity firm Avenue Capital has emerged as the leading bidder for a minority stake in the company that will hold the international media rights of Italy's top soccer league Serie A, two people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

Serie A is exploring the sale of a stake in a company that will hold its international broadcasting, sponsorship and betting rights and last month it received final bids from private equity firms.

Serie A clubs met on Friday for an initial review of the bids, the two people said.

New York-based Avenue Capital is targeting a stake of 10% in the media company for €320 million, the people said, which would put the overall valuation of the venture at €3.2 billion.

Avenue is in the lead despite the fact that some rival bidders have offered to pay more because its offer is structured as a common equity investment, without the protections on future cash flows sought by some of the competitors, one of the two people said.

The person added that Carlyle and Nextalia, which teamed up to submit a joint bid, had offered around €650 million for a stake of roughly 17%, valuing the venture at about €3.75 billion.

The Avenue Capital offer will be examined more closely in the coming weeks by the clubs, the people said, cautioning that there is no final decision on the matter.

Avenue Capital and Serie A declined to comment. Carlyle and Nextalia were not immediately available to comment.

Any deal requires the backing of at least 14 of the league's 20 clubs.

Home ⁠to Inter Milan, AC Milan and Juventus, the Italian league has been struggling in recent years to sell its media rights abroad, as broadcasters' interest ​dwindled due to a crowded fixture list dominated by the expanded UEFA ​Champions League and ⁠the popularity of England's Premier League.

The Serie A international media unit generates sales of around €250 million a year, a fraction of those yielded by Premier League and Spain's LaLiga, according to data from ⁠European soccer ​body UEFA.

(Reporting by Elvira Pollina; Editing by Valentina Za)

data.title: CoreWeave bond rout tests market's math on AI buildout
data.description:
PROVIDENCE, Rhode Island/NEW YORK, Oct 16 (Reuters) - A sharp decline in CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) bonds this week is emerging as a test of investors' willingness to keep financing the massive buildout of AI infrastructure, as rising borrowing costs and scrutiny of debt-funded expansion hit the sector.

Analysts and portfolio managers said the selloff in the data center operator's debt carries more significance than a concurrent rout in its shares because it may signal a broader reassessment of the risks tied to financing AI projects that may take years to generate revenue.

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) bonds issued in June at a yield of 9.675% have plunged in value, sending their yield to 15% this week.

"CoreWeave ( CRWV ) is absolutely the canary in the coal mine" for a market segment that is coming under more stress, said Max Frumes, global head of distressed and leveraged finance at 9fin, a fintech corporate credit data and analytics company.

"This is going to be a turning point in the pricing and availability and structure of credit that's supporting the AI boom," said Frumes, who believes that other AI-linked debt will follow CoreWeave ( CRWV ) into distressed territory. "It's going to get more expensive. There will be a lot more scrutiny and probably some pushback from investors."

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) shares fell 15.1% from Monday's open through Thursday's close, despite a 6% gain on Thursday after a vote of confidence from partner Nvidia. The decline was broadly in line with weakness in other so-called neocloud companies such as Nebius and Iren.

Credit investors said they already are becoming more selective.

"We're definitely taking another look at our exposures across the AI infrastructure space, particularly where the risks are concentrated and whether we're being adequately compensated for taking them," said John Han, a portfolio manager at fixed-income asset management firm F/m Investments.

F/m's portfolio contains unsecured CoreWeave ( CRWV ) bonds in one of its exchange-traded funds, but only because they make up part of the index tracked by the ETF. At their current yields those bonds "certainly deserve another look," Han said. He generally prefers to invest in high-yield securities via special purpose vehicles that may offer lower yields but also more collateral and less risk.

"The market is being very selective and really singling out anything that has more leverage, and (that may be) in a bit more challenging operating environment," said Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager of fixed income at Catalyst funds.

To Holzenthaler and other investors, what the markets are witnessing now is an overreaction as sentiment shifts from being overly upbeat to downright bearish.

In June, the risks driving the selloff -- the sheer size of the funding needs, the leverage, the reliance on outside financing, the risk that the GPUs (graphics processing units) being purchased for data centers would be obsolete before the new facilities could open -- were merely overlooked or downplayed.

"A few months ago, I would have said people were just too optimistic around AI," Holzenthaler said.

Deutsche Bank global head of macro and thematic research Jim Reid sees the market entering a new phase in which debt financing is becoming increasingly important.

"As we move to a capex cycle funded out of debt rather than simply free cash flow, we have to increasingly respect the credit price action," Reid wrote in a recent report. "AI financing costs aren't dramatic overall, but there are worrying themes at the edges."

Vanguard bond portfolio manager Brad Collins said assessing AI-related debt has become more challenging as issuers bring increasingly large and varied offerings to market, often forcing investors to make decisions in days or even hours.

Rising inflation has pushed financing costs higher overall and fueled concern about what lies ahead for mammoth AI capital spending plans. Then there is the growing political controversy surrounding the construction of data centers.

Even one of the tech sector's stalwarts allows that the road ahead may be bumpy at times. Dan Ives, partner and technology analyst at Yorkville Ives, an investment firm, estimates that 5% to 10% of planned projects ultimately will not be built.

"The growing noise around data center permitting and midterm rhetoric on power prices has given investors another reason to step back," Ives said.

(Reporting by Suzanne McGee in Providence, Rhode Island and Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss in New York; editing by Colin Barr and Cynthia Osterman)

data.title: US annual budget gap hits nearly $2 trillion, largest in 5 years
data.description:
* Debt-service outlays climb 12% to record $1.36 trillion, Treasury data shows

* Net tariff receipts fall $22 billion after $145 billion of refunds

* Fiscal 2026 deficit equals estimated 6.2% of GDP versus 5.8% in 2025

By Dan Burns

Oct 16 (Reuters) - The US budget deficit rose by $217 billion to nearly $2 trillion in the 2026 fiscal year, fueled in part by tariff refunds and record spending to service the nation's more than $40 trillion in debt, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years, Treasury Department figures showed on Friday.

Continued increases in spending for social benefits programs like Social Security and Medicare and a $48 billion jump in defense spending also factored into the increase.

The $1.99 trillion deficit for the year ended September 30, the first full budget year of President Donald Trump's second term, was up from $1.78 trillion in fiscal 2025. It was the largest shortfall since fiscal 2021's $2.77 trillion budget gap, then fueled by COVID-19 pandemic relief spending, and is the third-largest annual deficit ever.

Total receipts for fiscal 2026 were a record $5.40 trillion, up $169 billion, or 3%, from the $5.24 trillion in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 outlays also were a record at $7.40 trillion, up $386 billion, or 6%, from the $7.01 trillion in the prior fiscal year.

Debt-service outlays totaled a record $1.36 trillion, climbing by $144 billion, or 12%, a spending category now eclipsed only by Social Security and the combined outlays for Medicare and Medicaid. Total US debt breached the $40 trillion milestone about two months ago.

Another driver of the widening shortfall was a $22 billion drop in net tariff receipts following a Supreme Court ruling this year negating a large portion of the tariffs Trump had imposed during his first year in office. That triggered $145 billion of tariff refunds over this year, resulting in an 11% decline in net tariff income to about $173 billion.

Defense spending for the year rose by 6% to $917 billion. A US Treasury official said it was not clear how much of the increase could be attributed to the war Trump and Israel started against Iran earlier this year.

The Treasury official said the department calculated an estimated deficit-to-GDP ratio of 6.2% for fiscal 2026, but declined to say what GDP estimate was used. This figure compares to an actual 5.8% deficit-to-GDP ratio for fiscal 2025.

For the 2026 fiscal year's final month of September, the Treasury reported a deficit of $27 billion versus a $198 billion surplus a year earlier.

(Reporting by Dan Burns; Editing by Andrea Ricci)
